tasks.title: Your own function
tasks.statement: Define a function hello(name) that prints «Hello, <name>!», and call it twice: for «Ann» and for «Boris».
tasks.hint: def hello(name): print(f"Hello, {name}!") — and below it hello("Ann") and hello("Boris").

tasks.title: Average of three
tasks.statement: Write a function average3(a, b, c): the arithmetic mean of three numbers. The function must return the result, not print it.
tasks.hint: return (a + b + c) / 3 — it has to be return, not print.

tasks.title: Limit a number
tasks.statement: Write a function clamp(x, low, high): if x is less than low, return low; if it is greater than high, return high; otherwise return x itself.
tasks.hint: Two early exits: if x < low: return low; if x > high: return high; then return x.

tasks.title: Power with a default
tasks.statement: Write a function power(x, n=2): x to the power n. If n is not passed, square the number.
tasks.hint: return x ** n — the default value is already in the header.

tasks.title: Leap year
tasks.statement: Write a function is_leap(year): True for a leap year. A year is a leap year if it is divisible by 4, except for years that are divisible by 100 but not by 400.

tasks.title: FizzBuzz
tasks.statement: Write a function fizzbuzz(n): «FizzBuzz» if n is divisible by both 3 and 5; «Fizz» if only by 3; «Buzz» if only by 5; otherwise the number itself as a string.
tasks.hint: The strictest case first (both), then one at a time; at the end return str(n).

tasks.title: Kind of triangle
tasks.statement: Write a function triangle_kind(a, b, c): return «equilateral» if all three sides are equal, «isosceles» if exactly two are equal, otherwise «scalene».
tasks.hint: First check a == b == c, then “at least one pair is equal”: a == b or b == c or a == c.

tasks.title: Factorial with recursion
tasks.statement: Write a function fact(n): the factorial of n, but through recursion — the function must call itself. Base case: fact(0) = 1.
tasks.hint: if n == 0: return 1; otherwise return n * fact(n - 1).
